scope: Approved synthetic scenario, difficulty, and presentation-pacing parameters for the Phase 8 text-game package. This authority does not select physics equations, alter the approved solver contracts, or establish production/reference tolerances.

source_authority.coverage_reason: The draft selects gameplay timing, normalized state bands, deterministic seeds, command budgets, and loss-recording rules only; it does not select a reactor equation, physical constant, nuclear-data value, reference case, or golden numerical tolerance.

approval_must_confirm: The scenario identifiers, profile identifiers, seeds, and canonical seed derivation are frozen.
All timing values are gameplay seconds and all normalized fractions are unitless gameplay proxies.
The default interactive rate is 10 simulation seconds per wall second, capped at one simulation second per 100 ms presentation tick; real-time 1x remains available for inspection.
The wall control tick is presentation pacing only; existing explicit simulation and stable integration policies remain authoritative.
Player actions are acknowledged at the next wall control boundary and must not block on a long simulation solve; queue delay and commit timing are observable.
The initial-state mapping to the future Phase 8 runtime fixture is explicit and does not silently cross into a production CANDU data claim.
Command/event ordering, boundary inclusivity, rejected-command behavior, and loss-recording behavior are frozen.
Loss records terminate the game scenario only; no shutdown, scram, trip, safety-system, or accident progression is enabled.
P8-T02 owns the bounded runtime consumer; save/replay, scoring, and G8 evidence remain separate tasks.
owner_approval.promotion_rule: Promoted after explicit owner approval, the P8-T02 task report, the approved manifest hash, and the bounded runtime consumer were recorded.

seed_policy.seed_values_are: Scenario identity inputs, not physics or random-number evidence.
seed_policy.proposed_derivation: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 canonical seed input; the first eight bytes in little-endian order provide the replay seed.
seed_policy.repeatability_requirement: Identical parameter bytes, scenario identifier, difficulty identifier, seed, data-pack identity, and command stream must produce identical replay identity and outcome bytes.

units.time_s: Gameplay seconds; not a solver timestep authority.
units.normalized_power_fraction: Unitless gameplay proxy; nominal operating point is 1.0.
units.control_margin_fraction: Unitless gameplay proxy used only by the loss envelope in this draft.
units.command_budget: Count of accepted gameplay actions; not a physical device limit.

time_model.timing_policy: At each wall control tick, the presentation scheduler requests factor * elapsed wall time, clamps the presentation request to at most the declared presentation slice, and advances the explicit simulation clock through its existing deterministic event and integration policies. The presentation tick is not a physics timestep.
time_model.pause_policy: Pause stops simulation advancement at the next deterministic boundary and discards no accumulated state; wall-clock elapsed time is never replayed after unpause.
time_model.acceleration_change_policy: Acceleration changes are accepted only at an explicit simulation boundary, are recorded in the future replay stream, and do not alter any physical equation or integration substep.
time_model.responsiveness_policy: Player input is acknowledged immediately at the wall control boundary and is committed at the next valid simulation boundary; the future consumer must report queue delay instead of blocking the player on a long solve.

modes.intended_use: Default interactive play; maps 600/900/1200 simulation-second horizons to approximately 60/90/120 wall seconds.
Same stable rate as Play, with verbose event/replay diagnostics; no faster-than-approved mode is proposed.

grounding: The existing authority requires explicit discrete simulation time and prohibits Unity frame delta as physics time.
The existing synthetic RRS contracts use a 1.0 s cadence; the proposed 100 ms wall control tick and 10x playback rate expose at most one simulation second per presentation tick.
The existing P7 integration policy may subdivide a requested simulation interval into smaller stable substeps; the 1.0 s presentation slice does not replace or loosen that policy.
At 10x, the draft's 10/15/20 simulation-second decision intervals become approximately 1.0/1.5/2.0 wall seconds, avoiding long waits while preserving explicit event ordering.

base_fixture.description: Existing two-channel/three-position synthetic inspection fixture used by P8-T01.

scenarios.purpose: Teach inspection, waiting, a bounded target change, and one synthetic refuelling request without starting at an envelope boundary.
Exercise a centered power change while preserving zero initial tilt and a recoverable operating margin.
Exercise a nonzero initial regional tilt, a bounded corrective action, and deterministic recovery before the horizon.
Exercise deterministic channel/bundle request ordering under a limited command budget; this draft does not implement refuelling.
Verify inclusive boundary handling and a recorded gameplay loss when a target pushes the normalized proxy outside the approved draft envelope.

deferred_packages.scoring: Deferred to a separately bounded Phase 8 scoring task.
deferred_packages.save_load_replay: Deferred to a separately bounded Phase 8 persistence/replay task.
deferred_packages.runtime_command_consumer: Implemented by P8-T02 for approved scenario loading, deterministic seed identity, explicit time advancement, pacing modes, pause/resume, scripted proxy events, action queuing, and loss recording; save/load/replay/scoring remain separately bounded.
deferred_packages.long_run_soak: Deferred to G8 preparation and gate evidence.
deferred_packages.unity_presentation: Out of scope for this parameter authority.

approval_validation.requirement: UTF-8 JSON parses and required identifiers/status fields are present.
The future consumer regenerates identical replay identity from identical canonical inputs.
Minimum/maximum values are inclusive; only values outside the envelope create a loss record.
The operating-envelope scenario records loss without invoking shutdown, scram, trip, safety-system, or accident behavior.
A manifest binds exact artifact bytes, schema version, scenario/profile counts, and the owner decision before promotion.
